facts.heading: Exhausted per GP suggestion
facts.content: Daniel's general practitioner suggested he come because she said he looks exhausted.
facts.evidence: She said I look exhausted

facts.heading: Burnout started in October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burnt out since October.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burnt out since October

facts.heading: Workload increased after client loss
facts.content: Daniel's team lost a big client in October, leading him to do three people's jobs.
facts.evidence: We lost a big client, half of the team got moved onto the rescue plan

facts.heading: Works long hours
facts.content: Daniel starts work at 7 am and continues answering messages until 10 pm.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by 7 and I'm still answering messages at 10 that night

facts.heading: Sleep duration is about 4 hours
facts.content: Daniel sleeps about 4 hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about 4 hours

facts.heading: Wakes at 3 am unable to return to sleep
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at 3 in the morning and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: I wake up at 3 in the morning and just can't fall back asleep

facts.heading: Waking thoughts involve work
facts.content: When Daniel wakes at 3 am, he thinks about shipping schedules, the client, or forgotten items.
facts.evidence: Shipping schedules, the client, whether I've forgotten something

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: My father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn

facts.heading: Father's Parkinson's symptoms
facts.content: Daniel's father experiences shaking hands, slower movement, and frustration.
facts.evidence: His hands shake, he's slower, he gets frustrated

facts.heading: Daniel drives father to hospital
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to hospital appointments in Leeds every few weeks.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds

facts.heading: Caregiving is Daniel's sole responsibility
facts.content: Daniel is the one responsible for his father's care because his sister Hannah lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: all the care for our father falls of me

facts.heading: Daniel feels guilty about tiredness
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for being tired when his father is ill.
facts.evidence: He feels selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill

facts.heading: Daniel tells Hannah he is fine
facts.content: Daniel tells his sister Hannah that he is fine when she asks how he is.
facts.evidence: I say fine

facts.heading: Daniel wants Hannah to know he is not fine
facts.content: Daniel wishes Hannah knew that he is not fine.
facts.evidence: That I'm not fine

facts.heading: GP tests showed normal results
facts.content: Daniel's GP ran blood tests, and they were all normal.
facts.evidence: They were all normal

facts.heading: GP attributed issues to stress
facts.content: Daniel's GP said his issues were due to stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She said it's stress and exhaustion

facts.heading: Girlfriend Claire booked appointment
facts.content: Claire booked the appointment for Daniel because she was tired of seeing him disappear.
facts.evidence: A girlfriend booked her, to be honest. Claire. She said she was done watching me disappear.

facts.heading: Claire is patient with Daniel
facts.content: Claire is patient with Daniel and makes him tea without pushing him to talk.
facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Claire stopped weekend trips
facts.content: Claire stopped asking Daniel to go away for the weekend because he always said no.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend because I always said no.

facts.heading: Daniel avoids trips due to emails
facts.content: Daniel feels worst about his inability to say yes to trips because of the emails.
facts.evidence: The emails.

facts.heading: Daniel stopped running two months ago
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago.

facts.heading: Daniel ran for six years
facts.content: Daniel ran for six years before stopping.
facts.evidence: I've done it for six years.

facts.heading: Daniel feels loss of self
facts.content: Daniel feels like he has lost a part of himself since stopping running.
facts.evidence: Like I've lost a part of myself.

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails
facts.content: Daniel's boss, Peterson, sends emails at 11 at night and expects answers before breakfast.
facts.evidence: he sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Daniel answers boss's emails
facts.content: Daniel answers every email from his boss, even when he is not feeling well.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm not bad.

facts.heading: Fear of being seen as uncommitted
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that if he doesn't answer his boss's emails, the boss will think he isn't committed.
facts.evidence: Dan, he'd think I wasn't committed.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss during restructuring
facts.content: Daniel is afraid he might be let go due to a restructuring happening this spring.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring this spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Daniel has a mortgage
facts.content: Daniel has a mortgage.
facts.evidence: I have a mortgage.

facts.heading: Daniel experiences irritability
facts.content: Daniel reports feeling irritable, mostly while in his flat.
facts.evidence: Flat, mostly. And irritable.

facts.heading: Heart racing and shaking
facts.content: Daniel experienced his heart racing and his hands shaking while in a toilet for ten minutes.
facts.evidence: My heart was going and my hands were shaking.

facts.heading: Experienced chest symptoms
facts.content: Daniel experienced symptoms that felt like a heart attack, which later passed.
facts.evidence: I thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.

facts.heading: Prior chest symptoms
facts.content: Daniel has experienced this type of chest symptom a couple of times before.
facts.evidence: A couple of times.

facts.heading: Past chest symptom location
facts.content: One instance of the chest symptom occurred on a train to Manchester while standing on a platform.
facts.evidence: Once on a train to Manchester, just to get off and stand on a platform.

facts.heading: Avoided telling Claire
facts.content: Daniel had not told Claire about the chest symptoms.
facts.evidence: I hadn't told anyone about it, not even Claire.

facts.heading: Fear of losing control
facts.content: Daniel fears that the symptoms mean he is losing his mind or will end up coping poorly.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up, like, I don't know, coping.

facts.heading: Coffee consumption habits
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee per day.
facts.evidence: I want about six cups a day.

facts.heading: Evening wine consumption
facts.content: Daniel has started drinking wine in the evenings, consuming two to three glasses.
facts.evidence: And I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off. Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Waking up early
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at three in the morning.
facts.evidence: I wake at three anyway.

facts.heading: Difficulty sleeping
facts.content: Daniel feels that if he could sleep, he could cope with other issues.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think. If I could sleep, I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Family history of stoicism
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather worked at the mines in Yorkshire and never complained about anything.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked at the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything.

facts.heading: Belief about grandfather's view
facts.content: Daniel fears his grandfather would view him as weak for being in therapy.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.

facts.heading: Desired message to grandfather
facts.content: Daniel wishes he could tell his grandfather that he is not weak, but very tired.
facts.evidence: That I'm not weak. Just very tired.

facts.heading: Agreed to phone break
facts.content: Daniel agreed to try a small change: turning off his phone for 20 minutes in the evening.
facts.evidence: Yeah, half past nine perhaps.

facts.heading: Plan for phone break location
facts.content: Daniel plans to implement the phone break at the end of the sofa.
facts.evidence: I could make it a dangles glare. The end of sofa.

facts.heading: Plan to track sleep
facts.content: Daniel agreed to write down how the night goes upon waking up.
facts.evidence: I can do that. Right down when I wake up.

facts.heading: Current feeling after session
facts.content: Daniel feels tired but lighter after the session.
facts.evidence: Tired, but lighter.

facts.heading: Daniel's upcoming appointment
facts.content: Daniel plans to attend the next session next week.
facts.evidence: Same time next week?
